articles.title: Manchester United's Defensive Woes Continue Under Michael Carrick
articles.summary: Former Manchester United captain and current Sky Sports pundit Roy Keane has criticized Michael Carrick's leadership following the team's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa.
articles.content: Manchester United's defensive woes have sparked widespread criticism, and none more so than from a familiar face - Roy Keane. Keane, a former Manchester United captain and current Sky Sports pundit, unleashed a scathing attack on Michael Carrick's leadership following the team's 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford. The match was an eight-goal thriller that saw Aston Villa take a two-goal lead in just four minutes, leaving many wondering how the Red Devils would recover. United did stage a remarkable comeback to level the score before halftime but their fortunes took another downturn immediately after the restart, with Aston Villa taking a 4-2 lead. Keane's criticism of Carrick continued in his post-match interview, where he expressed frustration with the manager's vague statements. Keane claimed that Carrick talks a lot but doesn't say enough about the team's issues, saying "He keeps saying we need to tighten up and there's things we need to work on." The former captain emphasized that words are not enough, urging the team to take immediate action to address their defensive problems. The Manchester United squad has faced intense scrutiny following a dismal start to the season, with Keane pointing out the poor statistics. He questioned what specific changes Carrick and his coaching staff plan to implement in the coming weeks, demanding more concrete solutions rather than vague promises. Despite his harsh words, Keane acknowledged that the team showed resilience in their late fightback against Aston Villa, praising their determination to keep going despite a poor performance. However, he stressed that footballing ability is just as important as spirit, and the team needs to improve drastically if they are to succeed this season. The Manchester United team is facing an uphill battle this season, as evident from their recent performance against Aston Villa. The match was marred by defensive errors, which Keane described as "some bits so, so bad. Despite managing to salvage a point from the game, the overall display was far from satisfactory. The team's struggles have been well-documented, with many expressing frustration over their inability to hold onto leads. Matheus Cunha, one of United's forwards, captured the mood in the dressing room perfectly when he admitted to feeling so tired" and "so disappointed." His words reflected the collective sentiment among the players. The team's poor performance has left them languishing in the relegation zone, with only one Premier League victory this season. Their inability to fix their defensive issues is becoming a major concern for manager Michael Carrick. With each passing game, the pressure on him to improve the team's fortunes is mounting. A drastic change in the dugout may soon be on the cards if Carrick fails to address the team's weaknesses and instill confidence into his players. The club's hierarchy will be closely monitoring the situation, and a decision could be made to bring in fresh leadership to turn things around. articles.title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Lose 27-24 to Chicago Bears in Week 9
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell short of a comeback victory against the Chicago Bears due to their struggling offense despite forcing five total turnovers.
articles.content: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers suffered a heartbreaking loss to the Chicago Bears in Week 9, falling short 27-24 on a last-second field goal by Cairo Santos. In a surprising turn of events, the Bucs' defense transformed from listless to dominant after a lackluster first quarter, restricting Bears quarterback Caleb Williams to one of his worst performances in the NFL. The Buccaneers forced an impressive five total turnovers, including four crucial interceptions off Williams, which set the stage for a potential comeback. The momentum generated by the defensive efforts was unfortunately not matched by the offense, which struggled to capitalize on favorable field position despite reaching the red zone on 40% of its attempts. Additionally, Tampa Bay committed two costly turnovers that hindered their chances of success. A closer look at the game reveals an intriguing dichotomy between the Bucs' defense and offense. While the defense displayed a remarkable turnaround from their initial struggles, the offense was unable to translate defensive efforts into points, ultimately surrendering the game-winning field goal after the Bears' quarterback Caleb Williams had his worst outing in the NFL. The Bucs' pass offense struggled to capitalize on the numerous turnovers forced by their defense, particularly in the passing game. Despite completing 75% of his passes for 112 yards in the first two drives, quarterback Williams' accuracy and yardage plummeted significantly in the remaining part of the game. One notable aspect was the inability of the Bucs offense to convert interceptions into points, with Baker Mayfield's unit managing only three points off the five turnovers. Furthermore, they even surrendered a pick-six after picking off Williams for the fourth time, highlighting their struggles to capitalize on defensive efforts. The defense did its part in giving the offense one final chance to tie the game or take the lead, forcing a fumble by rookie outside linebacker on Chicago's 17-yard line with under four minutes left. The Bucs capitalized on this opportunity and tied the game at 24-24 after a Bucky Irving rush touchdown. However, the defense ultimately failed to hold up against the Bears' offense, allowing a long completion that put them in field goal range. This led to a 38-yard field goal by the Bears that sealed their victory with a score of 27-24. The struggles of the pass offense were particularly evident throughout the game, as they failed to live up to expectations despite the team's strong performance in terms of turnovers and defensive efforts. The Buccaneers' rushing game showed some signs of life despite not quite matching its previous performances. Bucky Irving was a bright spot in this area, managing to rack up 97 yards on 20 carries throughout the contest. Irving's efforts were also rewarded with two touchdowns for Tampa Bay. However, Kenneth Gainwell struggled to make an impact, gaining only 16 yards on five attempts. This limited his contribution to the team's overall rushing total of 28 carries against a more considerable number of pass plays. Baker Mayfield had some notable moments during the game, including a long completion to Tez Johnson that showed promise. Nevertheless, Mayfield was also responsible for several key mistakes that hurt Tampa Bay's chances. A late third-quarter interception by Jaylon Johnson proved particularly costly, ultimately sealing the team's fate in the loss. The Buccaneers' offense as a whole struggled with consistency and focus throughout the game, including issues on both sides of the line. The tight ends and offensive linemen committed five false start penalties, while receivers like Tez Johnson and Ted Hurst dropped crucial passes that could have made a difference. The Buccaneers' decision to give Baker Mayfield a $165 million contract before the season began has raised eyebrows given his performance so far. Mayfield's play this season has not justified such a massive payday, despite the fact that he is being paid like one of the best players in the NFL. He is expected to elevate the play of those around him, but his interceptions against the Bears look similar to those thrown by undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels earlier in the season. Mayfield's pick-six against the Bears ultimately made the difference in a one-score game, mirroring a similar mistake he made against Cincinnati. With limited easy completions from Zac Robinson, Mayfield is struggling to lead a winning offense, highlighting his individual limitations. articles.title: Northern Leaf Establishes Medical Cannabis Facility on Jersey Island
articles.summary: The company, Northern Leaf, has converted a 100,000-square-foot greenhouse on Jersey into a state-of-the-art operation for cultivating medical cannabis.
articles.content: A small island off the coast of England has emerged as an unlikely player in the global medical cannabis market. Northern Leaf, one of Europe's largest licensed medical marijuana producers, is based on Jersey, a British Crown Dependency. The company's 100,000-square-foot growing facility was previously used to cultivate tomatoes, which were once a prized crop on the island but are now struggling due to high production costs and cheaper imports from overseas. The greenhouse has been revamped with cutting-edge technology for cultivating cannabis that meets strict regulations for medical use. Automated irrigation systems, environmental monitoring equipment, and air purification units have transformed the facility into a state-of-the-art operation. Northern Leaf's CEO, Tan, is proud of what his company has achieved on this tiny island, which measures just 45 square miles in size with a population of around 100,000 people. Jersey lies only 14 miles off the coast of France but remains a British territory. Despite its small size and remote location, Jersey has become an important player in the medical cannabis industry, thanks largely to Northern Leaf's success. The company exports over 9,200 kilograms of cannabis annually, with the majority being shipped to the UK and Germany. The island's chief minister, Lyndon Farnham, has expressed his desire for Jersey to become a "centre of excellence for medical cannabis production. He wants cannabis to be a mainstay of the island's economy, and Northern Leaf is playing a key role in achieving this goal. The company currently accounts for 90 percent of Jersey's cannabis production. Northern Leaf's CEO, Tan, has ambitious plans to expand his operation further. He points out that the island's potato industry generates around £40 million annually, but he believes that cannabis production can match or even surpass this figure on a smaller scale. The island's unique geography and favorable business environment have created an ideal setting for Northern Leaf to thrive. Tan is confident that his company will continue to drive growth in Jersey's medical cannabis sector and establish the island as a leading player in the global industry. Jersey's unique regulatory environment has made it an attractive destination for businesses looking to capitalize on the growing demand for medical cannabis. As a Crown Dependency, Jersey has close ties to Britain but is not part of the UK, giving it the ability to make its own laws. This self-governing status has allowed the island to establish itself as a tax haven, attracting wealthy individuals and companies with its lack of capital gains tax and 0 percent corporation tax for most companies. The island's reputation as a hub for finance and wealth management is evident in its coastline, where offices of international banks and wealth management firms cater to the super rich. Alongside these high-end businesses are trendy beachside cafes and remnants of World War II history, including Nazi bunkers that occupied the Channel Islands during the war. Jersey's shift towards a more liberal approach to cannabis began with the legalization of medical marijuana in 2019. This move has paved the way for five private clinics to operate on the island, making it one of the leading destinations for medical cannabis treatment in Europe. The island's chief minister, Lyndon Farnham, had ambitious plans to establish Jersey as a hub of the medical cannabis trade. Farnham's vision involves repurposing the island's horticultural facilities and expertise from its previous tomato-growing industry to focus on medical cannabis production. This move has sparked interest among entrepreneurs looking to capitalize on the growing demand for cannabis-based products. The island's unique combination of regulatory environment and existing infrastructure makes it an attractive location for businesses in this sector. Jersey's decision to legalize medical marijuana has also attracted attention from companies looking to expand their operations into Europe. With its favorable tax regime and established financial services industry, the island provides a compelling proposition for businesses seeking to establish a presence on the continent. The growth of Jersey's medical cannabis sector is expected to continue, with several companies already investing in the island. Tan's company is one of the key players in this emerging industry, working closely with local authorities to drive growth and innovation. As the demand for medical cannabis continues to rise, Jersey is poised to become a leading player in the global industry. With its unique regulatory environment and established infrastructure, the island provides an attractive location for businesses looking to capitalize on this growing market. Northern Leaf's operations have been significantly boosted since Tan took over as CEO in 2024. Despite facing financial difficulties after a failed IPO, Tan has managed to increase production capacity from 25 percent to 75 percent over the last two years. The company's growth has been impressive, with Northern Leaf now capable of producing millions of units of cannabis. This surge in productivity is expected to continue, with the company aiming to export even more product in the future. One reason for Jersey's appeal lies in its unique regulatory environment. Growers on the island are subject to rigorous inspections by the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), which ensures that the highest standards of quality are maintained. This reputation for excellence is a major selling point for businesses looking to export cannabis products from Jersey. As barrister Sarah Clover notes, the MHRA's stamp of approval gives buyers confidence in the quality of the product coming out of the island. Clover, who works on cannabis licensing in Jersey, believes that the island has tremendous potential as a hub for medicinal cannabis production and packaging. With its existing facilities and infrastructure, Northern Leaf is well-positioned to take advantage of this opportunity. However, there are also challenges associated with running a cannabis business on a small island like Jersey. Local residents have expressed concerns about the smell of cannabis wafting from the facility and the potential impact on mental health. The issue of misuse has been highlighted by Jersey's health minister, who has noted that cannabis is a contributing factor in 22 percent of admissions to the island's acute mental health ward. While all of Northern Leaf's product is exported, some locals remain skeptical about the expansion plans. Medical cannabis has become increasingly popular on Jersey as a treatment for various ailments, including insomnia and anxiety. Patients like Michael have found relief from their symptoms after being prescribed medical cannabis by a specialist doctor. The process of obtaining a prescription is relatively straightforward, with patients meeting with a cannabis doctor who assesses their medical history. The initial assessment typically involves checking the patient's medical records with their general practitioner, and within 10 days, they are usually good to go. Michael was prescribed 30 grams of high-quality cannabis per month and was told that he could easily obtain more if needed. However, his experience ultimately ended in a negative outcome, as he found the medication affected his mental health. The availability of medical cannabis has led to an increase in user-dealers on Jersey, who sell their excess marijuana to others. This illicit resale has become a concern for those involved in the industry. Despite these challenges, the number of cannabis-related offenses on the island has dropped significantly since its legalization in 2019. According to statistics, there were 216 such offenses in 2016 but only 12 as of July this year. The overall decrease is seen as a positive outcome of the medical cannabis program. Tan, an industry expert, acknowledges that operating on Jersey can be difficult due to the local culture's resistance to cannabis. However, he attributes any pushback to his own experience and believes that people understand once they meet him. Tan has been in the industry for 25 years and is accustomed to facing challenges. His confidence in the medical benefits of cannabis remains unwavering. Some island residents are pushing for further decriminalization of cannabis use. In 2024, a vote to legalize recreational cannabis was narrowly defeated by a single vote in the parliament. The proposal was brought back up for debate but was eventually withdrawn before it could be discussed. The issue is expected to resurface in the coming months, with some individuals deciding not to wait for official approval. By exploiting a loophole in current laws, these residents have managed to purchase and consume THC products legally on Jersey. This development has made the island one of the few places outside of Amsterdam where such activities are tolerated. The situation on Jersey highlights the complexities surrounding cannabis legislation and its varying interpretations across different regions. As the debate continues, it remains to be seen how this issue will be resolved in the future. A Jersey weed shop owner has described the moment when a dozen customs officers raided his store in February 2024, seizing all his products. Gary Tucker's shop, Bailiwick Botanicals, is located in St Helier and sells cannabis-infused items such as hash cakes and gummies. The raid was not an isolated incident for Tucker, who has experienced similar situations before. He was taken aback by the scale of the operation, with officers emptying shelves and boxes into bin bags at a rapid pace. Tucker's products contain tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the psychoactive ingredient in cannabis that is heavily regulated. The shop owner operates outside Jersey's medical cannabis industry, which limits the sale of high-THC products to 3 percent of their weight in relation to CBD. To circumvent this restriction, Tucker boosts the CBD content in his products, essentially solving the problem with a math equation". Tucker admits that his solution is not ideal, as studies have linked excessive CBD consumption to liver damage. However, he maintains that he is simply catering to consumer demand and complying with Jersey's regulations. Tucker's cannabis products are currently manufactured in the US before being shipped to Sark, a Channel Island known for its car-free roads and autonomous government, and then on to Jersey. New regulations in the US may force Tucker to alter his production strategy, potentially disrupting his business model. Jersey is seen as a potential hub for exporting THC products to Europe, with Tucker believing that the island's fledgling cannabis industry should expand beyond medical use into the recreational market. Tucker claims that the cannabis industry has far-reaching economic benefits, creating jobs not just in cultivation and retail but also in related industries such as cosmetics and food production. articles.title: Nvidia CEO's Close Relationship with Megaspeed Executant Raises Security Concerns
articles.summary: US intelligence officials believe a senior executive at Megaspeed has been passing information to Beijing.
articles.content: A senior executive at Megaspeed has been embroiled in a controversy surrounding her alleged close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The New York Times reported last month that US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was passing information to Beijing, sparking concerns about potential security breaches. Megaspeed's ties to Nvidia have come under scrutiny before, as US authorities investigated whether the company and its Malaysian affiliate were helping Chinese businesses gain access to Nvidia's AI chips in violation of US export controls. It remains unclear when Huang first met Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, but public appearances suggest a close relationship between them. The Nvidia chief and Huang were spotted together at industry events, including a 2024 Computex Taipei trade show where they were pictured with other technology executives at a bar in a LinkedIn post from AI company NetThunder. A Taiwanese media outlet also captured footage of the pair leaving a Taipei restaurant alongside other executives in May 2025. These public appearances have raised questions about Huang's role and influence within Megaspeed, as well as her connections to Nvidia and its CEO. Despite these concerns, little is known about Alice Huang beyond her professional background and affiliations. Huang Le Limited, a company based in the British Virgin Islands, was granted ownership of Megaspeed's Singaporean entity after she took on the roles of director and managing director at the company. This transfer occurred just before Huang resigned from both positions on November 10, when Cang Yang also stepped down as a director. Corporate filings confirm this change in ownership. The handover of shares was part of a series of transactions involving Megaspeed's ownership structure. The Singapore entity is now solely owned by Swiftdata, another company incorporated in Singapore. This transfer took place on the same day that Huang Le Limited relinquished its stake, November 10. It appears that Swiftdata has maintained control over Megaspeed since then. Megaspeed was formed after 7Road International HK Limited split off its Singaporean subsidiary, according to reports. Prior to her time at Megaspeed, Huang worked as an executive director at a Shanghai investment fund with ties to state-backed companies and one that had backed 7Road. The investigation into Megaspeed by the Singapore Police is ongoing, but they have declined to comment further on the matter. Nvidia has maintained that Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were routine business dealings, and not unusual or unexpected. This assertion was echoed by John Rizzo, a company spokesperson, who stated that meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job and that Jensen talks regularly with thousands of customer executives every year. The Nvidia CEO himself addressed the situation in an interview with Bloomberg, stating that his relationship and interactions with Alice Huang were related to Megaspeed and completely normal. In a separate note to Nvidia staff on Sunday, Jensen admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, but did not mention Alice Huang or address their reported relationship directly.
